evidence: Turner specifically places Nepali hāmro, Awadhi hamar, Hindi hamārā and Bhojpuri hamār my in the extended asmāka possessive family. These Nepal/Terai hāmr-/hamār- forms match it, including nominative or singular usages in the survey; the Bhojpuri comparison already documents the shift to my.

Turner lists Nepali/Kumauni mero, Assamese mora/mohora, Oriya mohara and Old Awadhi moraü in the possessive series built on ma. These Nepal/Terai mer-/mor- survey forms match that documented adjectival possessive family, including ordinary gender-vowel variants.

Turner specifically gives Kumauni tumaro, Nepali timro, Bhojpuri tohār, Hindi tumhārā and Pahari tuãro in the possessive yuṣmad series. The Dotyali and Terai survey forms match these full tumar-/tohar- comparanda; contracted tor- forms are separated because they also match the singular possessive family.

Turner explicitly lists Apabhramsha tuhara and Bengali/Oriya tora among possessive derivatives of tuvam, beside Hindi terā. These short tor- singular/low-form Nepal/Terai possessives are assigned to that series; historical overlap with the plural tohar family is acknowledged rather than inferred solely from the generic your gloss.
